# Isolated responsive layout qualification

Run `node web-companion/frontend/scripts/serve-responsive-fixture.mjs` from the repository root, then open its printed loopback URL in a separate browser tab through CUA. The page automatically checks 50 combinations: gallery, Files, Settings, Jobs and preview at 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS pixels in both Light and Dark appearance. One real iframe runs at a time; its width sets the physical browser layout viewport. Use Inspect case to see any individual workflow.

The fixture loads the actual compiled Svelte shell, 60 actual compiled PhotoSummary components, imported current/legacy folder aliases sharing one opaque scope ID, retained workspace/panel/model-monitor controllers and the installed product styles. Each case receives its appearance attributes in server-rendered HTML before styles execute; the fixture appearance API reads and saves an in-memory value only. It replaces the engine bridge with synthetic in-memory records and cancelled file pickers. It never starts a companion, reads a user library/model or calls a native action. All resources are fixed at server startup, and the fixture's CSP prohibits external requests. Restart the server after changing styles or rebuilding the shell.

Checks cover document and uncontained horizontal overflow, actual visible control heights, Settings footer access, an independently scrolling gallery, preserved photo aspect ratio and node identity, plus drawer focus, inert state, Escape and backdrop dismissal. Gallery cases also exercise the actual Appearance menu through Light, Dark and Follow system with its mock persistence callback, expand/collapse filters, and change thumbnail density. The folder navigation must show one deduplicated root using its current source count, and library/header counts must update without a keyed-render failure. The standard task-action font assertion deliberately excludes sidebar navigation, whose smaller type communicates hierarchy; control-height minimums still apply to every visible control. The parent page exposes the results and saves `responsive-report.json` in its private output directory. This is browser layout and controller integration qualification; it does not qualify engine behavior, native pickers, real photo/model operations, assistive technology or physical touch devices. CUA screenshots and visual review are still required.
